claims.explanation: Triptolide covalently inhibits XPB/ERCC3, a TFIIH subunit required for RNA polymerase II transcription and nucleotide excision repair, causing rapid RNAPII degradation and apoptosis. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on high transcriptional output and intact apoptotic execution, so lines with wild-type TP53 and high MYC/transcription factor activity are sensitive, while those with mutations in apoptosis or DNA-repair effectors are protected.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines are enriched among least affected, consistent with impaired apoptosis after transcription blockade
XPB/ERCC3 is the direct triptolide target; higher expression may increase drug engagement and transcriptional dependence
MYC-driven transcriptional addiction increases dependence on RNAPII activity
BRAF-mutant melanoma and thyroid lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via MAPK-driven transcriptional output
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and lung lines are enriched among resistant lines, suggesting KRAS-driven survival signaling
SMARCA4-mutant lines appear in the resistant set, implicating chromatin remodeling in survival after transcription inhibition
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines and may reduce apoptotic priming
NFKBIA is downregulated by triptolide in virtual cell, and NF-kB inhibition sensitizes cells to apoptosis
RELA/NF-kB activity is inhibited by triptolide; high NF-kB may buffer against apoptosis
IAP family anti-apoptotic proteins can confer resistance to apoptosis induced by transcription inhibition
MCL1 is a key anti-apoptotic factor whose expression protects against apoptosis in cancer therapy
Caspase mutations impair apoptosis execution and are associated with chemoresistance
